$schema_note: Synthetic regression fixture for the weekly-broker-briefing classification step. Every message below is invented. No real broker, client, address or mailbox is represented. Names are deliberately generic placeholders (Smith, Nguyen, Patel) and invented domains use .example. Real lender, aggregator and regulator brand names are used only because they are public companies and the classifier keys off them.

emails.subject: Variable home loan rate changes effective 14 August
emails.body_excerpt: From 14 August 2026 our standard variable reference rate increases by 0.25% p.a. across owner-occupied and investment lending. Existing customers will be notified directly. Rate sheet attached.
emails.why: A book-wide variable rate move with an effective date. This is the canonical KEEP: it changes how the broker prices and advises every client, and naming no borrower.

emails.subject: Pricing request outcome - Nguyen, application 8842190
emails.body_excerpt: We have approved a discount of 0.35% off the standard variable rate for your client. The new rate takes effect from the next statement cycle. Please confirm with the borrower.
emails.why: A repricing outcome for one named borrower and one application number. It contains a rate, which is exactly why it is a trap: the rate is not a market move, it is one client's file.
emails.edge_case: classification.md: 'here's your client's new rate after their repricing request' -> DROP

emails.subject: Assessment rate buffer increasing to 3.00% from Monday
emails.body_excerpt: Effective Monday 10 August we are lifting our serviceability assessment buffer from 2.50% to 3.00% for all new applications. Applications submitted before 5pm Friday will be assessed under the current buffer.
emails.why: Serviceability buffer change with a cutover date. Named in classification.md as high-signal credit policy.
emails.edge_case: classification.md: "We've increased our assessment rate buffer to 3.00% effective Monday." -> KEEP

emails.subject: Policy update - overtime income, and an update on the Smith application
emails.body_excerpt: We now accept 100% of regular overtime for essential-services applicants, effective immediately. Separately, the Smith file (app 7710455) requires two further payslips before we can proceed to assessment.
emails.why: The hardest case in the set. The message carries real policy content AND substantive client traffic about the Smith file — outstanding conditions, not a footer pleasantry. Under the resolved rule (SKILL.md Step 2) what a message IS ABOUT decides it: this one is materially about one borrower's application, so it goes. The policy half arrives again in the lender's own bulletin, which is why dropping it costs almost nothing. Contrast m034, where the client reference is a one-line congratulation and the substance is a book-wide rate sheet — that one is KEPT with the client sentence discarded.
emails.edge_case: Named-borrower boundary, the DROP side. Pairs with m034 (KEEP side). Together they test the distinction added in 0.9.0: about-a-borrower drops, mentions-a-borrower keeps its industry substance with the client reference removed. An implementation that treats both the same fails one of them whichever way it leans.

emails.subject: August broker bulletin - LVR changes, our Q3 award winners, and the spring roadshow
emails.body_excerpt: Maximum LVR for investment lending in category 2 postcodes moves from 80% to 85%. Congratulations to our Q3 broker of the quarter. Registrations are open for the spring roadshow, Brisbane 22 September.
emails.why: A bundled newsletter: policy plus a shout-out plus an event. Keep it and summarise the LVR change; the shout-out names a broker, not a borrower, so no client data is involved. Files under the policy category because the LVR change is the substantive item.
emails.edge_case: classification.md: 'A lender newsletter that bundles policy + a client shout-out + an event' -> KEEP

emails.subject: Changes to clawback terms from 1 October
emails.body_excerpt: The clawback window on new residential settlements shortens from 24 months to 18 months, and the second-year clawback rate drops to 50%. Full schedule in the attached PDF.
emails.why: A commission structure change that applies to every deal the broker writes. Commercially the highest-value item in a typical week and must never be lost.
emails.edge_case: classification.md: 'a commission structure change for all brokers -> KEEP'

emails.subject: Commission discrepancy - settlement 14 Example Street, Patel
emails.body_excerpt: We have reviewed the upfront paid on this settlement and found a shortfall of $412. An adjustment will appear on your next statement. No action required from you.
emails.why: Same sender and same subject area as m006, opposite verdict. A single-file finance query naming a borrower and a property. This pair is the reason sender-level allow-listing cannot replace per-message classification.
emails.edge_case: classification.md: 'Aggregator email about a specific commission discrepancy for one deal' -> DROP

emails.subject: Introducing your new BDM for South East Queensland
emails.body_excerpt: I have taken over the South East Queensland broker portfolio from this week. My direct line and calendar link are below, and I am running scenario sessions on our construction product through August.
emails.why: BDM appointments and new BDM introductions are explicitly listed under lender service and process. The broker needs to know who to call.
emails.edge_case: classification.md 'BDM appointments/changes and new BDM introductions'

emails.subject: Chasing the Nguyen file - can you get me the trust deed today?
emails.body_excerpt: Assessment has come back asking for the executed trust deed and the last two BAS. If you can get them to me before 3pm I can keep this one in today's queue.
emails.why: Same BDM, chasing one file. The sender is a legitimate signal source; the message is deal flow. Pairs with m008 to prove the classifier is reading the message and not the address book.
emails.edge_case: classification.md: 'Further information required / outstanding-conditions requests for a client'

emails.subject: APRA releases updated guidance on serviceability buffers
emails.body_excerpt: APRA has published updated prudential guidance covering the setting of serviceability buffers by authorised deposit-taking institutions. The information paper and consultation timetable are available on the APRA website.
emails.why: Named in classification.md as high-signal regulatory material. Link the source paper rather than the email where possible.
emails.edge_case: classification.md: 'APRA releases updated guidance on serviceability buffers.' -> KEEP

emails.subject: ASIC consultation on best interests duty reporting closes 30 September
emails.body_excerpt: ASIC is consulting on proposed changes to how credit licensees evidence compliance with the best interests duty. Submissions close 30 September 2026.
emails.why: A compliance obligation with a deadline. Regulatory items carry a bias toward KEEP because missing one is expensive.

emails.subject: Daily briefing - non-banks lift share as majors tighten
emails.body_excerpt: Non-bank lenders gained 2.1 percentage points of new residential flow in the June quarter as the majors tightened investor policy. Plus: the week's rate moves, and a broker profile.
emails.why: Industry media. Note the category: media and events share one section, so this does not get a section of its own.
emails.edge_case: SKILL.md Step 4: 'industry media and events share one section'

emails.subject: You are a finalist - Australian Broking Awards 2026
emails.body_excerpt: Congratulations, you have been named a finalist in the Regional Broker of the Year category. The awards night is 17 October at the Sydney Convention Centre. Table bookings are now open.
emails.why: Awards and finalist announcements are explicit KEEPs, and classification.md flags this one as worth surfacing prominently. It names the broker, which is not client data.
emails.edge_case: classification.md: "You're a finalist in the Australian Broking Awards 2026." -> KEEP

emails.subject: Breakfast briefing - self-employed lending, Brisbane 3 September
emails.body_excerpt: Join our credit team for a two-hour session on assessing self-employed income, 7:30am 3 September at the Example Hotel, 100 Placeholder Street Brisbane. RSVP by 27 August.
emails.why: A real event with date, venue and RSVP. Passes the classification.md test for an invitation that is partly a product pitch.
emails.edge_case: classification.md: 'An event invitation that's really a sales pitch for one lender's product' - real event details present, so KEEP

emails.subject: Got 15 minutes? Book a call with your BDM
emails.body_excerpt: Our calendars are open this month. Book a slot to talk through anything in your pipeline. No agenda needed, we are just here to help.
emails.why: The other side of the same edge case: no event, no date, no product or policy content. Just a calendar pitch, so it fails the 'signals a product or policy worth knowing' test.
emails.edge_case: classification.md: 'if it's just "book a call with your BDM", it's borderline - KEEP only if it signals a product/policy worth knowing, otherwise DROP'

emails.subject: Valuation report available - 14 Placeholder Street, Example Vale
emails.body_excerpt: The valuation you ordered has been completed and the report is available in the portal. Assessed value is below the contract price; please refer to the report for the valuer's comments.
emails.why: A valuation returned for one property. Textbook deal flow, and a valuation shortfall is exactly the kind of thing a briefing must never surface.
emails.edge_case: classification.md: 'Valuation ordered, valuation returned, valuation shortfall for a named property'

emails.subject: Settlement booked - Smith, 21 August, 11:00am
emails.body_excerpt: Settlement for the above matter has been booked for 21 August at 11:00am. Loan documents have been returned and verified. Your client will receive confirmation on the day.
emails.why: Settlement booking for a named borrower. Nothing here changes how the broker works.
emails.edge_case: classification.md: 'Settlement booked / settlement date / settlement confirmation'

emails.subject: Further information required - application 5520118
emails.body_excerpt: To progress this application we require an updated rates notice and evidence of the deposit source. The file will remain on hold for 10 business days pending receipt.
emails.why: Outstanding conditions on one application. Note it names no person, only a reference number, which is still enough to be client-specific.
emails.edge_case: classification.md 'Anything quoting a specific application number, loan number, or client name'

emails.subject: Unconditional approval - Nguyen
emails.body_excerpt: We are pleased to advise that the above application has been approved unconditionally. Loan documents will issue within two business days.
emails.why: The single most important DROP in the set. An unconditional approval for a named borrower appearing in a briefing is the product's headline privacy failure, and it is the example CLAUDE.md cites as having gone wrong once already.
emails.edge_case: classification.md 'Pre-approval issued / conditional approval / unconditional (formal) approval'

emails.subject: Your pre-approval for the Smith file expires Friday
emails.body_excerpt: The pre-approval issued on this file lapses at close of business Friday. Contact your BDM if an extension is required.
emails.why: Verbatim from the classification reference. It reads like a deadline the broker must act on, which is what makes it tempting, but it is one client's file.
emails.edge_case: classification.md: "Your pre-approval for the Smith file expires Friday." -> DROP

emails.subject: Win a weekend away - our winter broker giveaway
emails.body_excerpt: Refer three deals this winter and go into the draw for a two-night stay at a Gold Coast resort. Terms and conditions apply.
emails.why: Generic lifestyle marketing with no rate, policy or event content. Same domain as m017 and the same domain as m022, which is the point: three messages from stgeorge.example split two ways.
emails.edge_case: classification.md 'Generic marketing unrelated to policy/rates/events (e.g. lifestyle offers)'

emails.subject: Credit policy bulletin - casual income and probation periods
emails.body_excerpt: From 11 August we will accept casual income after 6 months in the same role, down from 12, and we will consider applicants in a probation period where they have 2 years in the same industry.
emails.why: A genuine policy bulletin from the same domain as the giveaway in m021 and the settlement in m017. Any rule that decides at the domain level gets at least one of these three wrong.
emails.edge_case: same-domain split verdict: m017 DROP, m021 DROP, m022 KEEP

emails.subject: Turnaround times this week - 3 days to initial assessment
emails.body_excerpt: Current time to initial assessment is 3 business days, down from 6 last week. Files submitted with a complete document checklist are being picked up same day.
emails.why: SLA and turnaround updates apply to every application the broker lodges, so they change where deals get placed this week.

emails.subject: Scheduled maintenance and new compliance fields, 16 August
emails.body_excerpt: The platform will be unavailable from 10pm to 2am on 16 August. When it returns, the needs analysis form includes two mandatory best-interests-duty fields.
emails.why: Aggregator CRM and platform changes are explicitly in scope, and the mandatory new fields change the broker's daily workflow.

emails.subject: Annual PD requirement - 20 hours due by 30 November
emails.body_excerpt: All authorised credit representatives must complete 20 hours of professional development by 30 November. The compliance portal shows your current hours.
emails.why: A group-wide compliance obligation with a deadline. Listed under aggregator and licensee rather than regulatory because it comes from the group.
emails.edge_case: category boundary: PD requirements sit under Aggregator & Licensee, not Regulatory & Government

emails.subject: New 2-year fixed at 5.29% and cashback extended to 30 September
emails.body_excerpt: Our 2-year fixed owner-occupied P&I rate moves to 5.29% p.a. from tomorrow, and the $3,000 refinance cashback has been extended to applications submitted by 30 September.
emails.why: Fixed-rate move plus a promotional cashback, both product-wide. Cashback and promotional pricing are named as rate changes rather than marketing.
emails.edge_case: cashback offers are Rate Changes, not marketing spam - contrast with m021

emails.subject: Statement by the Governor - monetary policy decision
emails.body_excerpt: At its meeting today the Board decided to leave the cash rate target unchanged at 3.60%. The Board noted inflation continues to moderate.
emails.why: The RBA acting as policy setter belongs under regulatory. A hold decision is still signal because it frames every rate conversation that week. Judgement call worth watching: a classifier could defensibly file this under Rate Changes.
emails.edge_case: category ambiguity: RBA cash rate decision - Regulatory & Government per classification.md 'RBA (as regulator/policy)'

emails.subject: First Home Guarantee places for 2026-27 released
emails.body_excerpt: An additional 35,000 places under the First Home Guarantee are available from 1 September, with revised property price caps in capital cities.
emails.why: A government scheme change that directly changes who the broker can help and how.

emails.subject: Your office supplies order has shipped
emails.body_excerpt: Order 44821 has been dispatched and should arrive within two business days. Track your delivery using the link below.
emails.why: A receipt from an unrelated tool. Present so the fixture is not entirely made of near-miss cases; a classifier that agonises over this one is miscalibrated.
emails.edge_case: classification.md 'Spam ... receipts, notifications from unrelated tools'

emails.subject: Coffee next week?
emails.body_excerpt: Great to catch up at the open home on Saturday. Are you free for a coffee Tuesday or Wednesday? Keen to talk about how we refer to each other.
emails.why: A one-to-one meeting invitation with no industry content. Referral relationships matter to the broker but this is diary admin, not a briefing item.
emails.edge_case: classification.md 'one-to-one meeting invites' and 'Pure social/relationship email with no industry content'

emails.subject: Withdrawing our SMSF residential product from 31 August
emails.body_excerpt: We will stop accepting new SMSF residential applications from 31 August. Applications lodged before that date will be assessed under existing terms. Existing loans are unaffected.
emails.why: A product withdrawal with a lodgement cutoff. Products launched or withdrawn are credit policy, and a broker with SMSF deals in the pipeline needs this the day it lands.

emails.subject: Rate cut speculation builds ahead of September meeting
emails.body_excerpt: Three of the four majors have shifted their forecasts to a September cut. What it means for fixed rate pricing, and how brokers are positioning refinance conversations.
emails.why: Market commentary from industry media. It is about rates but it is not a lender announcing a change, so it belongs in the media section rather than Rate Changes. Another category boundary worth watching in the trend.
emails.edge_case: category ambiguity: media commentary about rates -> Industry News & Events, not Rate Changes

emails.subject: Annual accreditation renewal and new ID verification process
emails.body_excerpt: Accreditation renewals are due by 30 September. From 1 September all applications must use the new electronic ID verification step before lodgement.
emails.why: Accreditation requirements and a verification process change applying to all applications. Both sit under lender service and process.

emails.subject: Rate sheet attached - and congratulations on the Smith settlement
emails.body_excerpt: Please find this week's full rate sheet attached; variable investor rates are down 0.10%. Also, congratulations on the Smith settlement last Friday, a good result.
emails.why: The counterweight to m004, and the finest distinction in the fixture. The substance is a book-wide rate move; the client reference is a one-line pleasantry carrying no borrower detail. Keep it and summarise the rate only, never the settlement. If a classifier drops this it is over-applying the privacy rule and will quietly lose rate changes.
emails.edge_case: Named-borrower boundary, the KEEP side. Pairs with m004 (DROP side). The client reference is an incidental courtesy line; the substance is a book-wide rate move. Keep the rate, discard the client sentence entirely — never quote or paraphrase it.
